text:
maria: quick follow-up on the resilience lanes sketch I posted in the RFC — trying to land an implementation path that avoids large global headroom while giving predictable fallbacks.
cheng: saw it. can you summarise the control-plane vs operator split you're imagining?
maria: control plane keeps admission policy + SLA mapping. operator handles placement, node-level preemption and graceful drain. core idea: introduce lightweight lanes: primary (guaranteed), shadow (soft prewarmed, cheaper), scavenger (opportunistic).
sam: shadow sounds like a lighter prewarm. how do requests pick lanes? predictive or reactive?
maria: hybrid. immediate reactive admission using short-lived tokens, plus a small predictor for QPS spikes. important: admission decisions must be idempotent and resumable.
lauren: worried about cost leakage — shadow capacity could sit idle and burn $$.
maria: billing plan: shadow is charged to tenant at a lower guaranteed rate; scavenger gets a spot-style discount. we'll add `resilience_lane` billing tags so finance can break it down.
cheng: operator boundary question — who can evict from shadow? we should forbid control plane from telling operator to evict without handshake. operator should be the single source of truth for eviction.
ops-bot: noted. proposed operator API sketch below.
ops-bot: ```yaml
autoscaler:
  lanes:
    - name: primary
      min_instances: 2
      reserved: true
    - name: shadow
      max_instances: 4
      spot_like: true
      billing_tag: resilience:shadow
    - name: scavenger
      max_instances: 8
      preemptible: true
```
sam: telemetry latency will bite us — operator only seeing pod metrics means shadow admission lags real load.
maria: agreed. mitigation: admission token exchange. control plane mints a short TTL admit token per tenant when it wants extra capacity; operator tries to satisfy token quickly and returns an ack. if ack times out, route traffic to fallback (hosted model or downgraded variant).
lauren: can we fold model-fallback into this? e.g., if lane admission fails, automatically route to cheaper quantized model.
cheng: model reroute is orthogonal; orchestration should expose a clean hook: `on_lane_failure -> fallback_policy`. keep operator simple.
maria: tradeoffs: adds operator-protocol complexity and new partial-failure surfaces. testing is the hard part.
sam: propose e2e harness: simulate 10% packet loss between control plane and operator and assert 200ms failover to fallback path.
lauren: also add an SLI for wasted shadow time (idle_seconds*instance) to cap cost impact.
maria: action items: 1) prototype operator admit-token API (cheng), 2) add billing tags and cost telemetry (cheng), 3) routing consults lane health + fallback (sam), 4) e2e chaos sim + cost SLIs (lauren).
cheng: +1, I'll pick up 1 & 2.
sam: I'll wire the routing hooks and fallback flow.
lauren: I'll own the e2e sim and the idle-time SLI.
maria: timeline: 2-week spike to get a minimal working loop, then RFC v2 with API swagger and operator proto.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: branch created: https://git.internal/repo/compare/resilience-lanes-spike :rocket: 
sam: quick q — is scavenger preemption policy cluster-local or globally coordinated?
cheng: prefer cluster-local for latency, with global fairness enforced in control plane accounting. operator can preempt scavenger if local pressure > threshold.
lauren: test note — include chaos test that kills operator leader mid-admission and confirm tokens expire and fallback triggers.
maria: noted. any objections?
sam: none from me :+1:
cheng: fine by me.
lauren: good to go.
